title: **Règle canadienne du rachis cervical (Canadian C-Spine règle)**
short_title: **Règle canadienne du rachis cervical (Canadian C-Spine règle)**
formula: L’algorithme de questions Oui/Non de *The Canadian C-spine Rule* est plus performant que le jugement non structuré du médecin.

how_to_use.why:
- There are over 1 million visits to US Emergency Departments annually for blunt trauma patients who present with a concern for possible cervical spine imaging. Many of these patients undergo imaging of their c-spine, with the overwhelming majority (98%) of the studies coming back negative for a fracture. Applying the Canadian C-spine Rule would allow healthcare providers to safely decrease the need for imaging among this patient population by over 40%.
- While the Canadian C-Spine Rule is more complex than other c-spine clinical decision rules ( [NEXUS](nabda:calc.nexus-criteria-c-spine-imaging) ), it is a more sensitive rule and can potentially be used on patients who cannot be cleared using other rules.
how_to_use.when: La Canadian C-Spine Rule est une règle de décision bien validée qui peut être utilisée
how_to_use.pearls:
The Canadian C-spine Rule (CCR) was developed to help physicians determine which trauma patients need c-spine imaging.

- CCR is highly sensitive for CSI, with the majority of studies finding it catches 99-100% of these types of injuries.
- Applying the Canadian C-Spine Rule would allow healthcare providers to safely decrease the need for imaging among this patient population by over 40%.
- Subsequent studies have found a sensitivity of 90-100% for CSI with majority finding 99-100% sensitivity.

**Points to keep in mind:**

- Not all patients in the validation study underwent imaging if the treating physician felt the patient was at very low risk of injury.
- Most common criticism is that the CCR is difficult to memorize due to its multiple criteria; use of a smartphone app or digital reference (like MDCalc) is recommended.
- The rule *can* be used in patients who are intoxicated; if the patients are alert and cooperative, the rule can be used regardless of blood alcohol content.
- The quoted sensitivities are all for CSI. Some practice environments might be concerned with identifying **any** cervical spine injury (CCR is highly sensitive for clinically important c-spine imaging.)
- The lone trial with a sensitivity of 90% was in a study where nurses were trained to apply the rule (retrospective review by investigators in this study found the rule was misapplied in 4 cases with obvious high-risk features); it has also been successfully evaluated in paramedics.

**Exclusion Criteria:**

- Non-trauma patients.
- GCS <15.
- Unstable vital signs.
- Age <16 years.
- Acute paralysis.
- Known vertebral disease.
- Previous c-spine surgery.

next_steps.advice:
The overwhelming majority of patients who are CCR negative do not warrant further imaging.

- In the case of the inebriated but alert patient with a GCS of 15, one reasonable approach would be to leave the patient in a c-collar until they are clinically sober, however[one recent 2015 systematic review calls this into question](https://annals.org/article.aspx?articleid=2197180)assuming a high-quality c-spine CT study and an attending-level radiologist interpretation.
- The physician should order appropriate imaging when appropriate - XR vs CT - based on best clinical judgment.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Si un patient présente l'un des facteurs de haut risque (âge ≥ 65 ans, mécanisme dangereux défini ou paresthésies des bras ou des jambes), une imagerie de la colonne cervicale est alors nécessaire.
- Si un patient ne présente aucun facteur de haut risque mais ne remplit aucun des critères de faible risque définis (voir la liste), une imagerie de la colonne cervicale est nécessaire.
- Si un patient ne présente aucun facteur de haut risque, a une douleur cervicale, mais remplit ne serait-ce **qu'un seul** critère de faible risque, il est alors possible d'évaluer sans risque si le patient est capable de tourner son cou de 45 degrés vers la gauche **et** vers la droite. S'il y parvient (même avec une certaine douleur ou gêne), aucune imagerie complémentaire n'est nécessaire. S'il ne peut pas tourner son cou de 45 degrés dans les deux sens, des clichés de la colonne cervicale sont indiqués.
next_steps.management:
Si une lésion cliniquement significative de la colonne cervicale est identifiée à l’imagerie :

- Maintenir la protection de la colonne cervicale avec un collier approprié.
- Consulter la neurochirurgie.
- Garder le patient non ambulatoire et à jeun (NPO) jusqu’à ce que le plan de traitement soit complet.
- Le patient peut nécessiter une stabilisation chirurgicale en urgence et/ou une admission en USI neurochirurgicale.

evidence:
- Primary endpoint was clinically significant c-spine injuries.
- Validation study included a convenience sample of 8,924 patients, aged 16 to 64, presenting to 10 Canadian trauma centers, with stable vital signs and a GCS of 15. 1.7% of those studied had clinically significant c-spine injuries (CSI). CCR found to be **100%** sensitive for ruling out CSI (defined as any fracture, dislocation or ligamentous injury).
- Also detected 96.4% (27/28) clinically insignificant c-spine injuries (injuries that don’t require stabilization, specialized treatment and are unlikely to cause any long-term problems).

medium_description: Clinically clears cervical spine fracture sans imaging dans alert, stable traumatisme patients.

input_schema.name: age_65
input_schema.label: Âge ≥65 ans, paresthésies des extrémités, ou mécanisme dangereux
input_schema.tips: Fall from ≥3 ft (0.9 m) / 5 stairs, axial load injury, high speed MVC/rollover/ejection, bicycle collision, motorized recreational vehicle

input_schema.name: low_risk_factor
input_schema.label: Facteur de faible risque présent
input_schema.tips: Sitting position in the ED, ambulatory at any time, delayed (not immediate onset) neck pain, no midline tenderness. Simple rearend motor vehicle collision (MVC) (not simple if pushed into traffic, hit by bus/large truck, rollover, hit by high-speed vehicle)

input_schema.name: rotate_neck_45
input_schema.label: Capable de tourner activement le cou à 45° à gauche et à droite
